question: While testing the multi-agent research system, you see the error message "Citation source not found" in the logs of the synthesis subagent. The codebase of the system has hundreds of Python files, and you do not know which module raises this error or which functions call that code. Which use of the built-in tools is the most effective first step to locate the relevant code?

options.text: Use Glob to find files whose names contain "citation", then use Read on each matching file to look for the error message.
options.reason: The guide says Glob matches file paths by name or extension patterns, so it cannot find which files contain the error message text.

options.text: Use Read to load every Python file in the codebase upfront, then scan the loaded contents for the error message text.
options.reason: The guide says to build understanding incrementally, starting with Grep to find entry points, rather than reading all files upfront.

options.text: Use Edit with the error message text as the anchor, so that the tool reports which module contains a unique match.
options.reason: The guide says Edit is for targeted modifications using unique text matching, while Grep is the tool for searching file contents.

options.text: Use Grep to search file contents across the codebase for the error message text, then use Grep to find all callers of the function that raises it.
options.reason: The guide says to select Grep for searching code content across a codebase, for example locating error messages and finding all callers of a function.
